public_rationale: SoftBank confirms completed investment in October 2026, and OpenAI disclosed continuing cloud relationships. These records weigh against an imminent funding stop, but do not falsify an undated claim that support will eventually dry up. No event meeting the early-resolution rule was found.
limitations: Cloud access is not evidence of cloud credits.
The statement expresses concern about survival without predicting a specific failure event.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The flow of investment money and cloud computing credits to OpenAI will dry up, putting its ability to exist over the medium to long term in question.

statement.excerpt: Those two factors raise genuine questions about OpenAI’s ability to exist on a medium-to-long term, especially if — or, if I may be so bold to say, when — the sluice of investment money and cloud computing credits dries up.

from_speaker: the sluice of investment money and cloud computing credits dries up
ability to exist on a medium-to-long term
our_interpretation: The checkable commitment is that investment funding and cloud-credit support will eventually cease or become materially unavailable.
Questions about survival do not amount to an explicit prediction of bankruptcy.
Medium-to-long term does not supply a calendar deadline. The separate two-year hypothesis is not imported into this forecast.
A reduction in funding, a change of investor or paid access to cloud services does not establish the cessation of both forms of support.
No financial reporting basis, currency or amount is specified.
criteria.support_condition: Dated evidence establishes sustained cessation or unavailability of both investment funding and cloud-credit support.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event establishes that the forecast can no longer occur under its stated scope. Continued financing at a finite date alone cannot disprove an undated eventual prediction.
